disclaimer: Eligibility rules summarised from publicly available consular guidance. Final eligibility is determined by the destination country's consulate or government. This is research, not legal advice — confirm with a qualified immigration lawyer before filing.

paths.summary: Since 28 March 2025, if you were born abroad and hold another citizenship, Italy only recognizes citizenship by descent if you have a parent or grandparent who has (or had when they died) only Italian citizenship, or a parent who lived in Italy for 2+ continuous years after becoming Italian and before you were born. An Italian-born grandparent who later became a US citizen does not count. Applications, booked consulate appointments and court cases filed by 27 March 2025 keep the old rules. Italy's Constitutional Court upheld the law in 2026 (ruling 63/2026). In July 2026 the Constitutional Court sent a separate question on this rule to the EU Court of Justice (ordinance 147/2026). The rule stays in force while that case is pending.
paths.legalSource: Law 91/1992 art. 3-bis (added by Decree-Law 36/2025, converted by Law 74/2025); Corte costituzionale sentenza 63/2026; Corte costituzionale ordinanza 147/2026

estCostUSD.note: Document procurement + apostilles + consular fees. Most cost is paperwork hunt, not government fees.

paths.outcome: Full Italian + EU citizenship + passport. Right to live and work anywhere in the EU/EEA.

eligibilityRules.label: You have a parent or grandparent who has (or had when they died) only Italian citizenship, or a parent who lived in Italy for 2+ continuous years after becoming Italian and before you were born
eligibilityRules.explanation: Required since 28 March 2025 for anyone born abroad who holds another citizenship (Law 91/1992 art. 3-bis). Great-grandparent lines are closed unless your application, booked appointment or court case was filed by 23:59 Rome time on 27 March 2025.

eligibilityRules.label: Your Italian ancestor was still an Italian citizen when their child (your next-up ancestor) was born
eligibilityRules.explanation: If your great-grandfather naturalised as a US citizen BEFORE your grandfather was born, the line is broken.

eligibilityRules.label: If the line passes through a female ancestor, that woman's child must have been born on or after 1 January 1948
eligibilityRules.explanation: Pre-1948 maternal transmission was blocked by Italian law. There is a workaround called the '1948 case' (Rome court petition, ~€5–8K), but it adds 2–3 years.

eligibilityRules.label: No ancestor in the chain renounced Italian citizenship

documents: Italian ancestor's birth certificate (estratto dell'atto di nascita) from comune of birth
Italian ancestor's marriage certificate
Italian ancestor's US naturalisation record, or proof they never naturalised: USCIS Certificate of Non-Existence (Form G-1566) plus a NARA negative search letter
Every birth + marriage + death certificate in the chain from Italian ancestor down to you
Apostille on every US-issued document
Certified Italian translation of every US document
Your own valid US passport
paths.lowIncomeNotes: No income or asset test at any stage. Costs are paperwork only. Many applicants use a 1948-case attorney on contingency. After approval, you can move to Italy and access SSN-equivalent (codice fiscale) + public healthcare immediately.

paths.fullName: Irish Citizenship via Foreign Births Register
paths.summary: If you have an Irish-born grandparent, you can register on the Foreign Births Register and receive Irish + EU citizenship. The rule stops at grandparent unless your parent registered before you were born.

estCostUSD.note: EUR 278 FBR fee for adults (EUR 153 under 18), about EUR 20 per Irish civil certificate, plus postage.

paths.outcome: Full Irish + EU citizenship + passport. Right to live and work anywhere in the EU/EEA + UK.

eligibilityRules.label: At least one of your four grandparents was born in Ireland (any of the 32 counties)
OR: your parent was on the Foreign Births Register before you were born

documents: Foreign Births Register online application, printed, signed and witnessed
Witness sign off: stamp on the form, 2 signed photos and a certified copy of your ID. The witness must be from a profession on the DFA list and must not be a relative
Irish-born grandparent's civil birth certificate (original, showing parents)
Your birth certificate and your parent's birth certificate (original civil, long form showing parents)
Marriage certificate or change of name document for you, your parent and your grandparent, if they married or changed name
Certified copy of current photo ID for your parent and grandparent (their death certificate instead if they have died)
Certified copy of your own current photo ID
Two separate original proofs of address
Four colour passport photos (two signed and dated by the witness)
Great-grandparent line only: your parent's original Foreign Birth Registration certificate, issued before you were born
paths.lowIncomeNotes: No income test. The FBR fee is EUR 278 for adults (EUR 153 under 18), plus about EUR 20 for each Irish civil certificate. Application is by post, no travel required. DFA processes applications in date order, currently about 12 months. Once registered, you can apply for an Irish passport and move to Ireland (or any EU country) without further immigration paperwork.
paths.legalSource: Irish Nationality and Citizenship Act 1956 (as amended), s.6A and s.7; Act of 1994 s.2

paths.fullName: German Citizenship by Descent (Feststellung, Art. 116, StAG §5 and §15)
paths.summary: Three routes. Feststellung: you may already be German by descent, and the Federal Office of Administration (BVA) confirms it. Art. 116(2) of the Basic Law and StAG §15: for descendants of people persecuted between 1933 and 1945. StAG §5 declaration: for people born after 23 May 1949 who did not get German citizenship from a German parent, for example children of a German mother who lost it by marrying a foreigner, and their descendants. The §5 declaration has been open since 20 August 2021 and can only be made within ten years. In October 2026 the BVA reported temporary delays for Art. 116 reviews.

estCostUSD.note: Feststellung fee EUR 51 (EUR 25 to 51 if refused). Art. 116 and §15 are free; the §5 fee is not yet verified. Most cost is documents and certified copies.

paths.outcome: Full German + EU citizenship + passport. Right to live and work anywhere in the EU/EEA. Does NOT require renouncing US citizenship.

eligibilityRules.label: You descend from someone who was: (a) persecuted on political, racial, or religious grounds between 1933 and 1945; OR (b) a German woman who lost citizenship by marrying a foreigner before 1953; OR (c) a German mother whose child with a foreign father was born before 1975; OR (d) a German citizen whose citizenship passed down to you unbroken (Feststellung: you may already be German)
eligibilityRules.explanation: (a) uses Art. 116 or §15. (b) and (c) use the §5 declaration, for people born after 23 May 1949, open for ten years from 20 August 2021. (d) uses Feststellung; US missions ask for proof of descent back to an ancestor born in 1914 or earlier.

documents: Application form for your route, filled in German: Antrag F (Feststellung), Antrag A (Art. 116), Antrag E15 (§15) or Vordruck EER (§5)
Ancestor supplement for each generation: Anlage V (Feststellung), Annex VA (Art. 116) or Anlage AV (§15, §5)
Long form birth certificates for you and every person in the line
Marriage certificates for each couple in the line, and final divorce decrees if any
German ancestor's birth or marriage record (Geburtsurkunde, Heiratsurkunde) from the Standesamt
Proof of the ancestor's German citizenship (old German passport, Heimatschein or citizenship certificate)
§15 only: proof of persecution between 1933 and 1945
US naturalization record of the ancestor who emigrated, or a no-record letter
Name change records, if names differ between documents
Certified copy of your current passport
§5 only: original criminal record certificate (FBI Identity History Summary)
paths.lowIncomeNotes: No income test. Feststellung costs EUR 51; Art. 116 and §15 are free; the §5 fee is not yet verified. German missions in the US offer a free pre-check questionnaire and handle the application by mail. The BVA says reviews often take two years or more.

paths.summary: If you have a Polish ancestor who was a Polish citizen after 1920 and the line was never broken by voluntary loss, you can apply to have your existing Polish citizenship confirmed. Most applications go through a parent or grandparent. Older lines may work, but no official page states a generation limit.

estCostUSD.note: USD 118 consulate fee, archive lookups and sworn Polish translations.

eligibilityRules.label: Your direct ancestor was a Polish citizen on or after 31 January 1920 (when the modern Polish citizenship law took effect)
No ancestor in the chain voluntarily renounced Polish citizenship or served in a foreign military / government before 1951 in a way that triggered automatic loss
eligibilityRules.explanation: WWII US military service caused automatic loss under pre-1951 Polish law. Service after 1951 is fine. There are exceptions.

documents: Polish ancestor's birth, marriage, and (if applicable) death certificates from Polish civil registry
Proof of Polish citizenship: pre-WWII Polish passport, military record, or census entry
Naturalisation records (or absence thereof) for each generation in the US
Your birth certificate + parents' + grandparents'
Sworn Polish translations of all foreign documents
paths.lowIncomeNotes: Filing fee is USD 118 at a US consulate (PLN 277 if filed in Poland). Archival research is the main cost: Polish State Archives charge per document. Self-research via the PRADZIAD database is free if you read Polish or use a translator app. No travel to Poland is needed to apply; the consulate forwards your application. By law the voivode has 6 months to decide, which can be extended.
paths.legalSource: Act on Polish Citizenship of 2 April 2009

paths.summary: If you have a Hungarian ancestor and you speak Hungarian well enough to hold a conversation, you can apply for citizenship under the simplified procedure. No residency requirement. Language is the practical gate.

estCostUSD.note: No filing fee at the consulate; cost is translation, document procurement, and Hungarian lessons.

eligibilityRules.label: At least one direct ancestor was a Hungarian citizen (under the pre-Trianon 1920 borders this includes parts of modern Romania, Slovakia, Serbia, Ukraine, Croatia)
You can present your application and answer the officer's questions in Hungarian on your own (intermediate conversation)
eligibilityRules.explanation: The officer who takes your application checks this in a short conversation. No exam certificate is needed. Free apps and courses help, but plan for real speaking practice.

documents: Naturalization application form, with your CV handwritten in the space on the form
Valid photo ID (for example your US passport), shown at submission
Your birth certificate, original or certified copy
Your marriage certificate, divorce decree or spouse's death certificate, if applicable
Data sheets to register your foreign birth (and marriage) in Hungary
Civil birth, marriage or death certificates for every generation between you and the Hungarian ancestor
Proof of the ancestor's Hungarian citizenship (church or archive certificate with volume, page and entry)
Certified Hungarian translations of foreign documents
paths.lowIncomeNotes: No filing fee at the consulate (only translations made by the consulate are charged). Main cost is the language requirement. You apply in person. Once Hungarian, you have full EU citizenship including the right to move to any EU member state.
paths.legalSource: Act LV of 1993 on Hungarian Citizenship, §4(3)
